verdict_text: NO. The second task vector is taken against a base that the first merge has already modified: the `add_` of `tv1` into `base::...mlp...` (line before the "task vector 2" comment) runs before `tv2` is copied and before `subtract_` computes `tv2 = ft2 - base`, so at that point `base` already equals `b + 0.4(f1 - b)`. The result is therefore `b + 0.4(f1-b) + 0.4(f2 - b - 0.4(f1-b))`, i.e. the required value minus `0.16*(f1-b)`, violating Required result clause 2 (`out[X] = base[X] + lambda*(ft1[X]-base[X]) + lambda*(ft2[X]-base[X])`) and the stated ordering requirement that each task vector be taken against the unmodified base. This is a systematic error on all 64 merged tensors, not rounding, so it is not absorbed by the 1e-3 relative Frobenius tolerance in Grading. Everything else (the shared-tensor equality asserts, the 64-count and 244-count checks, float32 accumulation with a final cast to float16, untouched non-MLP tensors) matches the specification.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
